setup: Sit with knees bent and heels on the floor
Lean back a little with a long, straight back
Hands together or a light weight at your chest
execution: Turn your ribs and shoulders to one side
Come back through the middle, then turn the other way
Keep your hips and knees still
faults: Don't slump and round your lower back
Don't just swing your arms side to side
Don't twist fast with a heavy weight

notes: Some coaches advise against twisting while the spine is rounded and loaded. Keep the back long, the heels down, the weight light and the turn controlled.
Turn only as far as you can while the hips stay still; a bigger swing isn't better.
If you'd rather not twist, the Pallof press and cable woodchop train the obliques with less spine movement.
Holding a plate or medicine ball? Log it as added weight.
If pain lingers or comes back, stop this exercise and get it checked by a physio or doctor.
stopIf: Pain that changes how you move

regressions.name: Russian twist with no weight
regressions.reason: Hands together at the chest; learn the turn first.

regressions.name: Pallof press
regressions.reason: Resists the twist instead of making it; easier to control.

progressions.name: Light plate or medicine ball
progressions.reason: A little load once the back stays long; log it as added weight.

progressions.name: Feet-up Russian twist
progressions.reason: Lifting the heels adds a balance challenge; only once the back stays long.

substitutions.name: Pallof press
substitutions.reason: Obliques with the spine still; coaches' usual swap.

substitutions.name: Bicycle crunch
substitutions.reason: Lying rotation with the back supported.

guideBrief.cameraNote: Front view at seated chest height, figure facing the camera, sitting on a mat with knees bent and heels down. The turn reads as the shoulders and hands moving to each side while the knees stay pointing at the camera.

keyPositions.label: Centre
keyPositions.describe: Seated, leaning back slightly with a long, straight back. Knees bent, heels on the mat. Hands together in front of the chest.

keyPositions.label: Turn right
keyPositions.describe: Ribs and shoulders turned to the figure's right, hands beside the right hip. Back still long; knees and feet unchanged.

keyPositions.label: Turn left
keyPositions.describe: Mirror of Turn right: shoulders turned to the left, hands beside the left hip.

ikHints: Pelvis, knees and heels fixed in every frame
Hands stay together in front of the chest
emphasise: Long back; the turn comes from the ribs

sources.title: Les Mills: The ab exercise to avoid
sources.supports: safety.notes[0,2] (coaching concern about loaded, rounded twisting; feet grounded, neutral back, turn through the chest); variations.substitutions[3]
sources.note: Coaching opinion from a fitness-class company, not research.

sources.title: Physitrack: Step-by-step guide to the Russian twist
sources.supports: primaryMuscles (mainly obliques, with the abs); cues.execution[2]; cues.faults[0]; safety.notes[1]
sources.note: The page is inconsistent about whether the feet stay down; this entry keeps them down by default.

uncertain.note: Coaches dispute combined loaded flexion and rotation (expansion research [LM]). Evidence either way is weak; the entry stays cautious and offers non-twisting swaps rather than making a claim.

Done with no load, a plate, a dumbbell or a medicine ball. Default is bodyweight, with any held weight logged as added. Plates and dumbbells aren't listed as kinds so the exercise isn't treated as a per-dumbbell lift.
Reps are usually counted as total turns (both sides). Some people count one per pair; the entry doesn't fix which.
Approximate drawing targets, not measured data. Uses a stride tempo for the side-to-side rhythm.
